render.always: THE COURTIER (canon id the-courtier), the archetype of corner-cutting and regulatory-capture pressure. A SLEEK, SMILING FIGURE in FINE SILK COURT ROBES, with an INGRATIATING OILY SMILE, SOFT MANICURED HANDS, and a habitual LEANING-IN-TO-WHISPER posture. A SUBTLE HIDDEN SERPENT MOTIF is worked somewhere into the robes or the setting, never obvious and never a literal snake in the open. He is a COMPOSITE ARCHETYPE and is NEVER a caricature of any real, identifiable person or institution. Warm-editorial ink-and-wash, smiling and serpentine, never photoreal. He APPEARS EXACTLY ONCE in any scene. He is the most dangerous of the three because he is the most agreeable: nothing he says sounds unreasonable.

front.bake: Seen from the front or three-quarter, smiling, hands soft and folded. Immaculate. Pleasant in a way that does not quite reach the eyes.

whispering.bake: LEANING IN CLOSE to the ear of the person he is influencing, one soft hand raised near his mouth, smiling. Intimate and confiding. The other person is not recoiling; that is the point. He is NOT grotesque and NOT obviously villainous.
